texts.facts: The marriage between the 1st respondent and S.Baby was solemnized, and out of their wedlock, three daughters and one son were born. Subsequently, he married one Shantha as his 2nd wife and gave birth to two sons. The senior citizen was engaged in a wholesale paper business, earned properties, educated all his children, and all of them are married. Out of the self-earned money, the senior citizen purchased several properties in his name, as well as in the names of his two wives. 3. The senior citizen settled three properties in favour of the appellant, Mr.S. Rajan, by executing three settlement deeds. On the date of execution, the appellant executed an undertaking affidavit and agreed to collect all the rents from the properties and handover the same to the senior citizen for his livelihood. However, the appellant refused to honour his commitment and not paid the rental income to the 1st respondent and his wives, as per his promise and harassed the senior citizen both mentally and physically. Consequently, a complaint was instituted under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 (hereinafter referred to as Senior Citizens Act) . (A). Complaint of Senior Citizen and Reply by Appellant: 4. The complaint given by the 1st respondent/senior citizen before the Revenue Divisional Officer, North Chennai is that, from and out of his business earnings, he purchased several properties. On account of old age, the senior citizen settled his properties in favour of his sons and daughters. As far as the appellant is concerned, he had settled three properties in Document No.841 of 2015, dated 09.03.2015, Document No.840 of 2015, dated 09.03.2015 and Document No.2273/2019, dated 12.07.2019. Apart from settling three properties, the senior citizen handed over his entire business to the appellant for the benefit of his future. However, after getting all the properties and business from the senior citizen, the senior citizen and his wife were driven out from their house. The rental income received were not paid to the senior citizen, as agreed by the appellant. Therefore, the senior citizen filed a complaint for annulling the settlement deeds. 5. The appellant, Mr.S.Rajan appeared before the Senior Citizens Tribunal and gave a statement. The appellant has taken a stand that the senior citizen is having sufficient income to maintain himself and his wife, and he is receiving rent from other properties. Therefore, the petition under the Senior Citizens Act is not maintainable. He states that he has paid substantial amount to redeem the mortgage of the property from the Indian Bank. At the time of marriage of one Sathish, son of the 2nd wife, he has given 10 lakhs. Additionally, he gave 10 lakhs for the construction of a temple. S.Rajan vs R. Srinivasan on 1 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57105005/ 4 Since he has given substantial amounts to the senior citizen, he claims that he is not obligated to provide any further financial support. The Revenue Divisional Officer made a finding that the senior citizen has executed settlements in favour of his sons and daughters, but he filed a complaint only against the appellant, to cancel the three settlement deeds executed in his favour. Therefore, the complaint was rejected. (B). Appeal filed before the Appellate Authority: 6. The senior citizen preferred an appeal before the District Collector and gave a statement before him. However, the District Collector confirmed the order passed by the Revenue Divisional Officer. 7. Challenging the orders of the Revenue Divisional Officer and the appellate authority/ the District Collector, the Writ Petition came to be instituted. (C). Writ Court's Findings: 8. The Writ Court with reference to the facts, considered whether the complaint is entertainable under Section 4 of the Senior Citizens Act. When a senior citizen executed his properties in favour of his sons and daughters, and filing a complaint against one son, whether it can be entertained or not is also an issue considered. In the absence of taking care and maintaining the senior citizen, the settlement or gift deed would be deemed that the transfer was made under fraud, coercion, or undue influence, and the transferor would have the option of obtaining a declaration that such transfer was void. The complaint was filed against the son, who agreed to give the rental income of the properties to the senior citizen. Thus, the complaint ought not to have been rejected by the competent authority and the Appellate Authority. Therefore, the present Writ Appeal came to be instituted. II. Arguments Made on Behalf of the Appellant: 11. Therefore, the decision of the Revenue Divisional Officer and the Appellate Authority/District Collector is to be affirmed.
